task: inverse molecular design for catalysts and reaction-selective materials

claims.statement: Let tau pair mirror-image catalysts in a fixed achiral reaction environment, with a signed selectivity target y(tau(c)) = -y(c). If a candidate representation phi identifies the pair, phi(tau(c)) = phi(c), every deterministic predictor of the form f(phi(c)) has mean squared error at least y(c)^2 on the balanced pair, and signed-major-product accuracy is at most 1/2. Randomized predictors obey the same expected-risk bound.
assumptions: the target is signed product selectivity (for example, log(k_R/k_S) or signed ee), not its absolute value
the physical reflection exchanges product labels under a parity-even molecular model
the remaining reaction environment and conditions are achiral and fixed
the representation is exactly invariant across the mirror pair
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebraic obstruction is general and elementary; stereochemistry-aware selectivity prediction is established prior art. No catalyst discovery, chemical novelty, or priority claim is made. The contribution here is the explicit input/target contract and matched-pair discriminator.

costs.representation: Must preserve at least an orientation bit for signed mirror-pair outcomes; the bit does not determine selectivity magnitude.
costs.data: Requires absolute product-configuration labels and exact mirror-pair mapping.
costs.synthesis: Both enantiomeric catalyst identities, verified enantiopurity, and matched catalyst preparation are required; numerical cost is unknown.
costs.assay: Paired fixed-condition measurements of yield and signed ee or initial-rate ratio with replicate uncertainty; exact all-in cost is unknown.
costs.quantum_chemistry: If used, matched competing transition-state/conformer calculations and their spin/solvent/thermal model are additional costs; the theorem itself requires none.

claims.falsifier: The representation premise is falsified by showing phi(c) differs from phi(tau(c)); the physical reflection premise is challenged if verified mirror catalysts in an achiral, fixed environment reproducibly fail to reverse signed selectivity beyond assay uncertainty. A stereo-blind model cannot evade the theorem on fresh, leakage-free mirror pairs.
claims.next_gate: Run a blinded, randomized, replicate matched-enantiomer assay and compare otherwise identical stereo-blind and stereo-aware models on whole held-out pairs and scaffolds.

claims.statement: Under two-channel transition-state theory with equal pathway prefactors, ee = tanh(Delta/(2RT)) for Delta = G_S^‡ - G_R^‡. For a finite candidate set with a uniform estimation error bound |hatDelta_i - Delta_i| <= epsilon, the candidate maximizing hatDelta has regret at most 2 epsilon; hatDelta_selected - epsilon >= 2RT atanh(ee_target) certifies the signed ee threshold.
assumptions: two product channels, irreversible kinetic control, equal transmission/prefactors, fixed temperature
the selected candidate lies in the stated finite set
epsilon is a simultaneous uniform bound over the set, not a test-set mean error
claims.novelty_boundary: The TST conversion and argmax regret bound are standard consequences, not a novel catalyst-design algorithm. The result makes explicit the gap between regression error and a decision certificate.

costs.representation: Requires signed product labels, fixed reaction conditions, and a consistent barrier sign convention.
costs.model: Requires a uniform error guarantee on all candidate scores to certify selection; ordinary MAE/RMSE is insufficient.
costs.assay: Assay confidence bounds must be converted to the same signed Delta scale and combined with model error.
costs.quantum_chemistry: Barrier/conformer costs are task-specific and are not included in the algebraic certificate.

claims.falsifier: The physical conversion fails if measured outcomes are not governed by two irreversible channels with equal prefactors, for example due to different transmission factors, reversibility, product racemization, or changing catalyst speciation. The selection guarantee fails if the claimed uniform error bound does not hold on the finite candidate set.
claims.next_gate: For prospective campaigns, pre-register the signed endpoint and threshold, obtain simultaneous calibration or conservative error bounds, and report selected-candidate regret and hit rate at equal assay/synthesis budgets.

claims.statement: A current source-reported mechanism-aware Ni catalyst-design workflow maps a supplied ligand library into TSRC/intermediate/TSRE templates, computes xTB-refined conformationally informed features, and combines a literature-pretrained model with EDBO+; its prospective benzylic-acetal coupling study reports about 70,000 geometries over 195 ligands in about two weeks and 26 experiments over four rounds at fixed reaction conditions, reaching maximum DeltaDeltaG^‡ = 0.98 kcal/mol (68% ee).
assumptions: statement is attributed to the cited paper and not independently rerun in this track
the reported computational campaign uses supplied reaction/mechanism templates
reaction conditions were not varied in the prospective campaign
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a reconstruction of primary-source reported work, not a new result. It establishes a strong baseline and exposes the supplied-template and fixed-condition boundaries. No equal-total-cost comparison against the strongest alternative acquisition method was independently reproduced here.

costs.candidate_space: 195 chiral N,N ligands; about 47% reported commercially available.
costs.quantum_chemistry: Approximately 70,000 geometries in about two weeks; xTB optimizations/refinement, filtering and clustering, PCM/omegaB97X-3c single points; 756 descriptor summaries per transition state or intermediate.
costs.synthesis: Noncommercial selected ligands require multistep synthesis; exact time, cost, failure, and purification burden are not established in the main article.
costs.assay: 26 prospective experimental screens in four rounds, conditions fixed; exact all-in assay cost and aggregate failure accounting unknown here.
costs.mechanism_template: TSRC/intermediate/TSRE template and reaction-specific mechanism are supplied; acquisition and validation costs must be charged for a new reaction.

claims.falsifier: An exact rerun with the published data/code that fails to reproduce the reported geometry counts, screen sequence, or measured candidate ranking would contradict this reconstruction; a new prospective test that misses the selected-candidate target would falsify transfer to that new task, not the original source report.
claims.next_gate: Benchmark EDBO+ against equally informed random, nearest-neighbor/fingerprint, and simple mechanistic-regression acquisition under identical candidate, literature-data, synthesis-feasibility, and wet-assay budgets; separately include condition optimization.
